tob-10785: Written by a colleague of Freud and Jung, this pioneering work argues that the strange symbols of alchemy — furnaces, kings, dragons — are really pictures of the human mind at work. Silberer reads alchemical texts as early attempts to describe psychological transformation. The book became a bridge between occult tradition and the new science of depth psychology.
tob-4085: Yeats’s 1903 book marks his turn from dreamy romance to a harder, plainer note. The title poem and its fellows draw on Ireland’s hero-age — Cuchulain and the old tales — while facing a present-day Ireland he found thin. The book stands at the hinge of his life’s work.
tob-0085: Fathered on the medieval schoolman Albertus Magnus, this spell-book of homely magic hoards charms, receipts, and privities for health, love, and warding. Handed down for centuries, it weds book-magic to peasant slyness. The book is a peephole on the people’s sorcery.
tob-4285: Budge’s Gods of the Egyptians — book one — is the great muster of Egyptian god-lore, naming the gods, their tales, and their worship. The British wonder-house’s Keeper of Egypt wrote with unmatched weight. The work opened old Egypt’s faith to common folk. A monument of young Egypt-lore.
tob-10485: Benedetto Croce’s Mystics of the Renaissance — in Frasci’s translation — studies the Italian mystics and what they mean for modern thought. The great thinker’s essays link Renaissance holy life with present-day ideas. The work is a fine piece of thought-history.
memoirs-of-sir-wemyss-reid-1842-1885: T. Wemyss Reid, the noted journalist, looks back on his busy life from 1842 to 1885 — newspapers, politics, and the literary world he knew. His memoirs are full of good stories and shrewd judgments. A lively Victorian self-portrait. Editors, statesmen, and men of letters pass through these lively, well-told recollections.
the-renascence-of-hebrew-literature-1743: Nahum Slouschz tells how Hebrew woke from sleep between 1743 and 1885 — poets and thinkers of the Haskalah giving new life to an old tongue. His book was the first to chart this rebirth for scholars. A landmark of Jewish literary history, still cited.
arxiv-2605-08785: Video playback and AI inference tolerate small arithmetic errors if the chip runs faster and cooler for it. Pragun Jaswal, L. Hemanth Krishna, and B. Srinivasu design a reconfigurable multiplier for the open RISC-V processor core that dials precision up or down depending on what the application can stomach. The 2026 paper is hardware research aimed at thriftier, cheaper silicon.
arxiv-2605-08885: Foundation models for chemistry must respect rotation — a molecule's energy does not change when you turn it — which is what SO(3) equivariance guarantees. Chen Wang, Siyu Hu, Guangming Tan, and Weile Jia make such atomistic models compact through structural pruning, cutting size while keeping the symmetry. The 2026 paper targets lean, physics-honoring models of matter.
arxiv-2605-08985: Multimodal models that see in ultra-high definition drown in pixels; encoding them efficiently is the bottleneck. Kechen Fang, Yihua Qin, Chongyi Wang, and colleagues ask what actually makes visual encoding efficient in the fourth version of LLaVA-UHD. The 2026 paper dissects efficient vision for multimodal LLMs.
arxiv-2605-09085: Estimating probability densities comes in two flavors — continuous and discrete — usually handled separately. Zhijun Zeng, Yixuan Jiang, Pipi Hu, and Zuoqiang Shi unify them with constant-target energy matching. The 2026 paper is a single unified framework for both worlds of density estimation.
arxiv-2605-09185: AI trading agents will face liars — fake news, planted rumors — and someone must test their gullibility first. Zhiwei Liu, Yangyang Yu, Yupeng Cao, and colleagues build AutoRedTrader, which red-teams trading agents by injecting synthetic misinformation. The 2026 paper is adversarial testing for financial AI.
arxiv-2605-09385: Tensor networks simulate quantum systems, but loops make truncation treacherous — naive cuts destroy the physics. arxiv-2605-09885: The spin Seebeck effect converts heat into spin current; compensated ferrimagnets in magnetic junctions host it in intriguing ways. Xin Theng Lee, Takahiro Misawa, Mamoru Matsuo, and Takeo Kato investigate. The 2026 paper is spintronics on heat-driven spin currents in junctions.
arxiv-2605-09985: Humans compress abstractions prospectively — anticipating what will be needed before it arrives. arxiv-2605-10085: Accessible communication in a mixed-ability non-profit — designing for collective access, not individual accommodation. Xinru Tang and Anne Marie Piper search for solutions. arxiv-2605-10185: Ghost imaging — reconstructing images from light correlations — made dynamic with quantum detectors and temporal transformers: DynGhost. arxiv-2606-16985: Daniel Waxman and Dmitry Batenkov release Dynestyx, a software library for probabilistic programming applied to dynamical systems, models of things that change over time, from epidemics to machinery. arxiv-2606-17085: Emilio Santos reformulates quantum field theory in the Weyl-Wigner representation, a phase-space picture where quantum states look like classical probability clouds with negative patches. arxiv-2606-17185: T. arxiv-2606-17685: Yue Chang demonstrates coherent control of an embedded bound state without a spectral gap. The fragile state hides inside a continuum yet can still be steered with light. The result defies the intuition that bound states need isolation to survive.
arxiv-2606-18185: Michał Trojanowski and Michał Wojtylak design an encoder-transformer architecture for recognizing the Jordan structure of a matrix. arxiv-2606-18285: Vaibhav Balloli and colleagues curate and evaluate reproductive health information on social media with RELIANCE. arxiv-2606-18485: Subhankar and colleagues generate long-form speech at inference time without training on long-form data with MagpieTTS-LF. plos-pone-0003385: Not all body fat behaves alike, as this 2008 obesity study shows. plos-pone-0003785: McGowan, Hogg, and Campbell brought librarians to the exam room in this 2008 trial. Their just-in-time information service fed rapid research answers to primary-care doctors during patient hours. The randomized test showed timely evidence sharpening everyday medical decisions.
plos-pone-0003885: Working in 2008, a team linked a virus to meningitis bacteria in young adults. A bacteriophage, a virus that infects bacteria, was found associated with meningococcal disease. The phage connection suggests the usually harmless throat germ turns nasty with viral help.
plos-pone-0003985: In 2008, Tokuda, Jimba, and Yanai linked trust to well-being in Japan. Their cross-sectional study tied interpersonal trust to quality-of-life scores. plos-pone-0004085: In 2008, Eldin, Ismail, and Mansour tracked acute hepatitis C in Egypt. They measured spontaneous viral clearance after symptomatic acute hepatitis infection. A delayed 12-week treatment course was also tested. The careful study guides when to treat and when to wait.

plos-pone-0004685: In 2009, a team tested new bone drugs against breast tumors anew. New bone drugs curbed breast cancer growth and spread. The new drugs beat older bone drugs cleanly. The study offers a therapy lead today. The bone pull was strong.
plos-pone-0004785: In 2009, Jäncke, Koeneke, and Hoppe mapped the skilled golfer's brain anew. The architecture of the golfer's brain was charted. Long practice reshaped brain structure deeply. The study maps expert neuroscience wiring. The brain alterations are practice-dependent indeed here.
plos-pone-0358885: Athletes stretch three ways — dynamic, static, and PNF — but which actually extends range of motion? plos-pone-0357185: When teenagers in France develop mysterious fatigue and pain, Lyme disease often gets blamed — rightly or not. plos-pone-0357285: A child’s hearing loss caught late can cost them language itself. This study surveyed mothers of 1–5-year-olds on their knowledge and attitudes about childhood hearing loss. The gaps it found show where awareness campaigns must go to catch deafness early.
plos-pone-0358485: Tyrosine kinase inhibitors keep myeloproliferative neoplasms in check — but only if patients take them. plos-pone-0353485: The Herculaneum scrolls — carbonized by Vesuvius — may hold lost classical texts. plos-pone-0357785: Spotting behavior disorders in preschoolers starts with asking parents the right questions. plos-pone-0357585: A high AUROC score can mask catastrophic decision failures in medical AI. plos-pone-0355285: Enzymes can be harnessed to destroy pharmaceutical pollutants in water. plos-pone-0352885: Ancient metalwork along the Amber Road corridor traces the birth of elites. This paper followed socioeconomic change and emerging elites in the 4th–3rd century BCE through their metalwork. The artifacts map how power concentrated — written in bronze, gold, and iron.
plos-pone-0356285: High-fat diet mice develop the nerve damage of diabetes — a crucial model for testing treatments. plos-pone-0357385: Repeated exposure to the pesticide methyl bromide damages nerves and muscles. This paper studied the neuromuscular effects of that repeated exposure in detail. The findings quantify an occupational harm that regulators and farmworkers need to confront with hard numbers.
plos-pone-0356785: Thriving in the digital age demands soft skills, emotional intelligence, cognitive flexibility, and self-directed learning — but how do they connect? plos-pone-0356485: Germany’s approved digital health apps (DiGAs) are often evaluated with ultra-short questionnaires. plos-pone-0356885: Vascular dementia’s cognitive fog might lift with help from a traditional Chinese medicine compound. plos-pone-0354585: Spiramycin antibiotics polluting waterways need breaking down — and light plus catalysts can do it. plos-pone-0356685: Half-million-volt DC cables live or die by their electric field distribution. This paper examined how semiconductive shielding protrusions disturb the field in ±500 kV HVDC cables. The findings guide cable manufacturers toward designs that won’t fail catastrophically under load.
plos-pone-0355685: Antenatal care saves newborn lives — but which models work best in poor countries? plos-pone-0356385: Deep UV light can stiffen soft silicone — a useful trick for microdevices. This paper characterized the stiffening using nanoindentation. The precise mechanical measurements let engineers tune silicone stiffness with light — patterning hard and soft regions on a single chip.
plos-pone-0355385: Median U-turn intersections — replacing direct left turns — are spreading, but their performance across traffic levels needed testing. plos-pone-0353785: Everyone has frustration triggers — but they differ wildly between people. plos-pone-0355485: Diagnosing tuberculous pleurisy — TB fluid around the lung — is notoriously difficult. plos-pone-0354385: Geothermal fields of medium and low temperature — like Wenquan County’s — form through mechanisms worth understanding. This paper investigated their genesis mechanisms in Xinjiang. The geological findings guide the hunt for clean geothermal energy in similar terrains.
plos-pone-0354885: Four dengue serotypes circulated together across Mexico from 2020 to 2025 — a complex co-circulation. This space-time scan analysis mapped their spatiotemporal patterns. plos-pone-0354485: Emergency departments miss HIV — unless testing is guided by indicator conditions. plos-pone-0341285: Noncommunicable diseases — losing the media agenda to COVID-19. This paper examined news coverage before and during the pandemic. The findings document how the world’s biggest killers vanished from headlines — and the framing responsibilities journalism abandoned.
plos-pone-0353985: India’s marine microbiome — hiding antimicrobial peptides against drug-resistant ESKAPE pathogens. This paper identified and biophysically characterized candidates in silico. plos-pone-0354185: Refractive index sensing — highly sensitive — via asymmetric TiO2 grating response under LED light. This paper built it. The nanophotonic sensor detected minute index changes cheaply. The findings democratize precision sensing — laboratory sensitivity from LED illumination.
plos-pone-0353685: Generative AI in higher education — stakeholders’ discourse mapped by topic modeling and sentiment analysis. This paper did so. plos-pone-0352585: UAV-assisted sparse ground networks — modeled and analyzed. This paper did so. The analysis revealed how drones fill connectivity gaps. The findings guided the aerial infrastructure — wings as network towers.
plos-pone-0353385: Youth elite soccer players — GPS-derived acceleration-speed regression lines’ reliability and validity. This paper tested them. plos-pone-0353885: Glycemic meritocracy in sport — between lay expertise and medical recognition. This paper explored that tension. plos-pone-0351885: Telemedicine’s global inequities — mapped through an umbrella review of barriers and facilitators. This paper synthesized the syntheses. plos-pone-0353185: Digital use across generations — intergenerational patterns from a large cross-sectional study. This paper provided the evidence. The findings mapped how age shapes screen life. plos-pone-0352985: Pit and fissure sealants — material type, salivary contamination, and adhesive application effects on performance. This paper tested them. The analysis found what makes sealants fail. Its clinical value is the child’s molar. The work keeps the sealant sealed, despite the spit.
plos-pone-0351985: Joint pattern classification and reconstruction — top-down and bottom-up attention. This paper built the model. The architecture looks both ways at once. plos-pone-0343485: Japanese large-footed bats — avoidance of simultaneous patch use. This paper documented it. The analysis revealed the bats’ foraging etiquette. Its behavioral value is the spacing. plos-pone-0352785: Palestinian health sciences students — AI knowledge, attitudes, and practices in a cross-sectional study. This paper did so. The analysis surveyed the future clinicians’ AI readiness. Its education value is the baseline. The work asks the students about the machines.
plos-pone-0352185: Desert sensor nodes — passive thermoelectric temperature regulation optimized for dust resilience. This paper did so. The analysis hardened the electronics against the dunes. Its engineering value is the endurance. The work keeps the sensor cool where the sand blinds.
plos-pone-0350885: Paenibacillus polymyxa CACC1094 from bovine rumen — broad-spectrum antifungal activity and genome-guided characterization. This paper did so. europmc-pmc2808385: Some people with HIV make antibodies that kill many strains, a gold clue for shots. europmc-pmc2914085: Chiefs cannot wait years for proof roundups. This 2010 paper looks at fast-track reviews, how they are done, and what they risk. The authors weigh haste against care in method. Their take guides quick yet honest evidence for busy decision-makers.
europmc-pmc2919785: Dogs vary wildly in shape, yet the genetics are simple. This 2010 paper shows a simple genetic architecture underlies morphological variation in dogs. The authors find a few genes explain much of the difference. Their work made dogs a model for gene mapping.
europmc-pmc3004885: Bacterial genomes need crowd-scale study. This 2010 paper brings BIGSdb, a database for comparing germ genomes across whole populations. The authors' tool became a typing staple. europmc-pmc3044685: Celiac and arthritis share gene spots. This 2011 gene trawl finds fourteen shared risk spots outside HLA in the two diseases. The authors reveal the overlap. Their work points to shared therapies. One pill might calm both conditions. The immune system misfires in similar ways.
europmc-pmc3045385: Stressed leukemia cells shed decoy bubbles. This 2011 paper shows heat and oxidant stress makes blood-cancer cells shed immune-dulling bubbles. The authors reveal the decoys. europmc-pmc3074985: Sharp minds can harbor Alzheimer's plaques. This 2010 paper finds amyloid buildup in cognitively healthy elders. The authors reveal the paradox of reserve. europmc-pmc3079585: The genome got a user's guide. This 2011 ENCODE guide explains the encyclopedia of DNA elements. The consortium demystified the genome's dark matter. europmc-pmc3146885: Ancestry testing got faster math. This 2011 paper speeds up the ADMIXTURE tool for reading individual ancestry. The authors cut run times sharply. Their software spread through genetics. Thousands of genomes process in hours. The tool powers ancestry tests. It is open source.
europmc-pmc3153485: Bacteria's starvation alarm got mapped across life. This 2011 paper traces the RelA/SpoT protein family across all domains. The authors reveal the ancient family tree. europmc-pmc3161885: Lactic acid tamed bad vaginal bacteria. This 2011 paper shows lactic acid, not peroxide, suppresses vaginosis-linked bacteria. The authors overturn an old belief. europmc-pmc3198985: Calcium chatter near cell power plants got reviewed. This 2011 paper covers calcium signals around mitochondria-linked membranes. The authors map the crosstalk. europmc-pmc3247885: Fast-track joint surgery's delays got studied. This 2011 paper asks why patients linger in hospital after rapid-recovery joint surgery. The authors reveal the reasons. Their work guides discharge planning. Pain and dizziness topped the list. Better protocols cut stays further.

europmc-pmc3358085: E. coli resistance got a 50-year count. This 2012 paper tracks E. coli drug resistance from 1950 to 2002. The authors reveal the rise. Their work pushed action. Farm use drove the rise. Tadesse's team led the work. The paper is widely cited.
europmc-pmc3362085: Tumor marker studies got REMARK. This 2012 paper explains the REMARK reporting rules for tumor markers. The authors elaborate the guidelines. Their work guides researchers. europmc-pmc6524685: Every branch of life - archaea, bacteria, and eukaryotes - sheds tiny membrane bubbles into its surroundings. europmc-pmc6645485: When researchers rate the same thing twice - or compare raters - the intraclass correlation (ICC) measures agreement. europmc-pmc6653385: Some dying cancer cells do the immune system a favor - dying in a way that sounds the alarm.
